data.definition: The development and validation of instruments to assess students' self-efficacy in engineering-related tasks, including programming, design, and general engineering skills. This theme consolidates self-efficacy measurement with broader engineering competencies, emphasizing its role in professional development and skill acquisition.

data.theme: Motivational and Learning Strategies in Engineering Education
data.definition: The validation and adaptation of instruments to measure students' motivational attitudes, learning strategies, and engagement in engineering education. This theme focuses on the psychological and pedagogical factors influencing student performance and persistence in engineering programs.

The development and validation of instruments to measure entrepreneurial mindset constructs (e.g., 'Connections' and 'Creating Value') and design mindset in engineering students. This theme captures the intersection of innovation, creativity, and problem-solving in engineering education.

The adaptation and validation of instruments to assess students' perceptions of their internship and workplace experiences, including competencies developed and satisfaction with training. This theme bridges academic learning with professional practice.

The assessment of systems thinking skills and problem-solving competencies in engineering students using surveys and diagnostic activities. This theme emphasizes the ability to analyze complex systems and develop effective solutions.

The development and validation of instruments to measure workplace oral communication skills and other communication-related competencies in engineering students. This theme focuses on the practical application of communication in professional engineering settings.

The development and validation of instruments to assess mathematical and technical competencies in engineering students, including the use of Rasch analysis and think-aloud protocols. This theme addresses foundational and advanced technical skills critical to engineering practice.
